note: Default settings for the build loop. A project's own .claude/workflows/loop.config.json (written by the build-loop skill's setup) is laid over these key by key; args passed to a run override both. Every value has a Why beside it, and a project's file should keep that habit.
ownerWhy: Who a run hands back to. Setup writes the maintainer's name.
baseBranchWhy: The branch a run starts from and opens its pull request into. Setup reads it from the remote's default branch, or an integration branch such as staging or develop when the repo has one.
branchPrefixWhy: Every run works on <prefix><slug> in its own worktree, never in the maintainer's checkout.
protectedBranchesWhy: No agent pushes to these, opens a pull request into them, or checks them out. The base branch is allowed unless it is listed here.
commitStyleWhy: type(scope): subject. Many release tools read it. Set to "plain" if the repo doesn't use it.
commitTrailerWhy: A line every loop commit ends with, such as a Co-Authored-By line. Empty adds none.
modelWhy: No override: each role uses its model below. args.model forces one model for every agent.
modelsWhy: The cheapest model each role's work allows. Haiku only relays script output. Sonnet runs checks and commits, writes the retro, reads official docs, builds tasks with no screen, access, API or risky path, and runs the gates that read logs and docs. Opus takes the judgement: the spec, readiness reviews, the security and UI gates, design previews and design research, fixers, the approver, and any builder whose task has a screen, a design risk, auth, the API or a risky path. A builder that returns nothing or stops part way is retried on the strong model. The cost report records each agent's model, so the retro can move a role up when its first-pass findings rise.
maxParallelWhy: Agents at once. More than this runs through a usage allowance before any of them reports.
effortWhy: Builders, integrators and gates at medium; the spec, fixers, reviewers and the approver at high.
useAgentTypesWhy: Rules live in .claude/agents/loop-*.md and the guard hook, where a run's prompt can't override them. Set false only in the session that installed the agent types, which can't see them yet.
turnCapWhy: A builder past about this many tool calls stops and reports where it got to; its agent type's hard limit is higher, so it always has turns left to report.
fixerTurnCapWhy: Fixers read the most per agent. Small fixers grouped by file, then the lead.
maxFixRoundsWhy: One round, then the lead. A second round rarely fixes what the first could not and costs as much again.
budgetTokensWhy: Context tokens one run may read. Over it, the build pauses after a wave and fix rounds stop; the same slug resumes.
abandonedLockMinutesWhy: A run's lock counts as abandoned when its heartbeat is older than this.
auditEveryWhy: Run the loop in audit mode after every few feature runs, so debt already in the code shows up before a person finds it.
softCapsWhy: Each role stops at about this many tool calls and reports what it has; every agent type's hard maxTurns is at least 15 above it.
stackWhy: What setup found: languages, the package manager, and each dependency that shapes how code is written, with its installed version and its official docs. Builders follow these frameworks' conventions for the installed version.
projectDocsWhy: The repo's own rules (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, architecture notes). Every agent treats them as the law.
writingGuideWhy: The repo's guide for words people read, if it has one. The copy gate judges against it.
readinessWhy: The bar every change is held to. Setup writes it from the template, cut to this stack.
readingWhy: For each area a task can name, the doc sections a builder of that area reads, as "path#Heading". Keys are the areas the spec may use. A short start is the biggest saving there is: a builder's tokens are mostly its context re-read on each turn.
worktreeWhy: Untracked files a run needs (env files) and the install command, from the lockfile.
checksWhy: Every deterministic check, run by scripts/loop/checks.mjs before any gate agent reads a line. Each is { name, command, when?, files? }: `when` is a pattern a changed path must match for the check to run at all; `files` is a pattern that picks the changed files substituted for {files} in the command. Setup copies what CI runs, so the two never disagree.
builderChecksWhy: Fast checks a builder runs on its own files only, with {files} for them: a linter with fix, the unit tests near them. Never a full build, typecheck or e2e run.
ciWhy: "github" pushes the branch, opens a pull request and reads its checks with the gh CLI. "none" skips the CI stage, and the tests gate runs tests.e2e itself. workflowFile and projectPattern let the loop notice a test suite a task added that CI never runs.
testsWhy: The commands that run end-to-end tests, and unit tests related to changed files ({files}).
screensWhy: How to take screenshots, or null for a project with no screens: { baseUrl, start, roles: { name: storageStatePath | null }, widths, themes, themeCookie, command }. With no `command`, scripts/loop/shoot.mjs drives the repo's own Playwright install.
designWhy: The project's design docs, where its best screens are listed, the design-reference tools this machine has (MCP tool names, found by setup), and a design critique skill if one is installed. Without reference tools, design research uses web search and the project's own screens.
approveWhy: "hand-back" never merges: the approver writes its verdict on the pull request for the owner to decide. "merge" lets it merge into the base branch when every check passed and the risk check found nothing, then wait for deployWorkflow, check versionCheck ({ url, pattern }) and run the smoke command against the deployed site. A failure there gets one fix round, then the approver reverts its own merge.
riskPathsWhy: Changed paths that always go to the owner, by area (access, money, data). Patterns are regular expressions matched against every changed path that isn't a doc or a test.
migrationsWhy: A pattern matching migration files. A migration matching dataChangingSql goes to the owner.
dataChangingSqlWhy: A migration that changes existing data goes to the owner. Adding a table, a nullable column, an index or an enum value doesn't.
heavyCommandsWhy: Each starts a server, a browser, a full build or a database job. Only gates, integrators, fixers and the approver run them, one at a time under the machine's heavy lock. Setup adds the project's own (its dev server, build, e2e and typecheck scripts).
approverCommandsWhy: Anything other people see or that changes a shared branch. The workflow pushes the branch and opens the pull request itself (ship.mjs pr), so CI can run before the approver decides.
roleCommandsWhy: Outward commands one other role may run, as { "loop-<role>": [command] }.
forbiddenWhy: Anything that throws work away or reaches production, a shared database or a release. Setup adds the project's deploy, release and production database commands. Pushes to protected branches are refused from protectedBranches.
